opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. opportunities.title: Model fiat currencies and multi-chain token bindings as domain state
opportunities.summary: ## Background The Banking Ledger must distinguish internal fiat-denominated balances from external tokens used for blockchain settlement. An intermediate redesign removed the `Currency` aggregate and introduced a statically injected `SettlementAssetRegistry`. That model has important limitations: - supported currencies and token bindings are queried directly from runtime configuration instead of being reconstructed as Read Models from domain events; - one Currency effectively resolves to only one deposit token and one withdrawal token; - chain identity is hidden behind Solana infrastructure types; and - completed Deposit and Withdrawal aggregates do not retain the blockchain transaction that produced the settlement. Replace the static registry with event-sourced Ledger domain state. Restore `Currency` as a bank-managed aggregate, model multiple token bindings as entities owned by that aggregate, make the supported blockchain explicit in domain values, and project the resulting events into normal Read Models. opportunities.title: [feat] Retrieval-augmented remediation: few-shot self-repair from the journal's outcome-verified fixes
opportunities.summary: ## Problem / motivation When the self-healing loop (#2830) sends an agent to patch a blamed node, that agent starts cold — it re-derives a fix from scratch even though the org's journal very likely contains a **past failure of the same shape that was already successfully fixed**. #2411 surfaces the *previous attempt* within the same run, but nothing generalizes *across runs*: "this failure looks like one we solved three weeks ago in a different workflow — here's what worked." opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
